blind.why: Main menu at 1920 (g_main_1920.png) vs a CS2 squad-lobby frame (reference/cs2/ss_0.jpg). In CS2 five large, distinct, warmly lit agents fill about 70% of the frame height, centred and facing the camera. Our line-up is about 17% of the screen height and squeezed into the gap between the nav list and the Match Setup panel. Two Tide athletes sit under the PRACTICE RANGE/LOCKER text, more are ghosted behind the panel, and a stray red/blue vertical bar still floats above the ring.

Video tab at 1920 vs CS2 Video settings (oneesports capture). Ours has a clearer hierarchy: framed sheet, preset cards with a per-preset spec grid, a live fps/draw-call readout and a one-line description on every row. CS2 has more granular controls but looks flat. Ours only shows about 5 rows per screen and needs a MORE pill.

Recap after a real 12-round bot match, Tide 8-4 (f_m_recap_1920_1280.png), vs the CS2 Premier post-match rating reveal. Ours tells you what happened: two tables, MVP and award cards, and a round strip with a halftime divider. CS2 gives the stronger emotional moment (agents and points banner). Ours has no hero or celebration and no 'your progress' beat.

Audio tab at 1920 vs CS2 Audio settings. Ours has 4 sliders with TEST buttons, dashed level meters that never move, and about 60% of the panel empty. CS2's tab has substance: device, EQ profile, L/R isolation, voice and push-to-talk options.

biggest_gap: The main-menu showcase, which is the first thing a player sees, is the weakest screen and loses to the CS2 lobby. Repro: load http://localhost:5173/ with no ?test and wait for main, or see g_main_1920.png, g_main_3840.png and fr_1280_t18000.png. (1) The six athletes stand only about 180px tall at 1080p, roughly 17% of viewport height, and are crammed into the roughly 700px gap between the nav column and the Match Setup panel. The two left Tide athletes render under the 'PRACTICE RANGE' and 'LOCKER' labels, and more athletes plus a third of the ring sit behind the translucent setup panel. (2) A stray red/blue vertical bar floats above the ring at top centre (about x 940-1000, y 0-230 at 1920). It was flagged in r3 and is still there; it looks like map geometry leaking into the showcase. (3) Several athletes face sideways or away and one crouches pointing a tagger at its neighbour, so they don't read as a posed squad presenting to the camera. CS2 stages five large agents centred, lit and posed toward the viewer, and its UI frames them instead of covering them. Fix: move the camera in and reframe so the squad fills the centre band (athletes at 40% or more of viewport height), between the nav and the panel with no overlap. Remove or cull whatever draws the floating red/blue bar. Turn the poses to the camera with one hero in front.
other_gaps: Main-menu keyboard focus is ambiguous. 'PLAY MATCH' keeps its full orange 'selected' bar permanently, while the item that actually has keyboard focus (for example SETTINGS after ArrowDown x3) gets only a faint dark box with a thin orange tick (crop_kbd.png, t_kbd3.png). Two items look selected at once. CS2 highlights only the hovered or focused entry.

Audio tab is thin: 4 sliders, level meters drawn as dead dashes that never animate, about 60% empty panel (g_settings-audio_1920.png). There is no output device, mute-when-unfocused or music-kit/round-music toggle.

Settings density at 1920: rows are about 89px tall, so only 5 controls fit per screen and every tab needs scrolling or the floating MORE pill. On Video, Colour-blind sits below the fold at 1280. CS2 fits 8-10 rows. The Viewmodel preview is still a schematic grey wedge on a sky card, not the real viewmodel.

Recap round strip is hard to read. Chips are coloured by final squad but the legend reads '◆ Ember ◆ Tide'. In the real match the first four chips are cyan with 'B' (beacon), which reads as 'Tide won by Beacon' even though only attackers can win by Beacon. The B/E/D/T letters have no key. The credit and timeline line chart has no axes or labels and adds little.

Recap has no 'you' beat. The local player's row is just a slightly lighter row at the bottom (0/4/0 here), with no personal summary such as ADR, best round or MVP stars, and no hero or celebration moment like CS2's post-match agent line-up and points banner.

Real-time first run on this shared software-GL box (about 0.7 fps on the menu): the pause card twice appeared with its four buttons missing or unhittable for several seconds, the pause #1 card stayed at opacity 0 for at least 4.5 s, and one Play transition frame showed the closed Settings sheet over the live HUD (f_16_leaving, f_r_pause0/1, f_09_trans300). I could not reproduce any of this deterministically (3x pause/resume in ?test is clean), so it is most likely raster starvation. The pause UI does depend on opacity/visibility transitions plus animation delays, so a long hitch hides it.
strengths: True first run (no ?test): splash, then a branded boot bar with stages (Loading typography, Compiling shaders, Staging showcase, Profile), then main with no key press, then Play, then a match with 10 actors, a tutorial card and the HUD. A full real 12-round match reached matchEnd, the recap appeared, and Main menu returned to a working main. The only console errors came from my own listener.

Settings really apply. Verified: FOV 110 horizontal gives camera vfov 77.55 at 16:9. Rebinding jump to J makes J jump (vel.y 3.1) and Space stops jumping, and the tutorial card and F1 cheat-sheet show J. Quality Low switches render.quality and the shadow map to 1K at 85% scale. HUD scale 130% visibly enlarges the HUD, the Dot crosshair shows in game, and Deuteranopia recolours team UI in game.

Leave match is fixed and fully keyboard-driven: Esc, ArrowDown x3 to Leave, Enter opens the confirm with Stay focused, ArrowRight then Enter leaves to main. Esc on the confirm means Stay. Repeated pause/resume keeps Resume focused and all buttons hittable. tools/menu_flow_test.mjs is extended with these checks plus FOV and rebind-applies, and all 22 checks pass.
The layout scales cleanly through --u at 1280, 1920 and 4K with no clipped text. Pause, settings, cheat-sheet and recap all hide the HUD correctly, and Tab scoreboard layers over the tutorial card.
The recap has a clean hierarchy: DEFEAT/VICTORY title, a two-team table, award cards, and a halftime divider in the round strip.
